message: Insecure Database Configuration: Use of DriverManagerDataSource

title: Open Redirect
message: Open Redirect

title: Incomplete Proxy Interface Implementation
message: Incomplete Proxy Interface Implementation

title: Potential Format String Injection
message: Potential Format String Injection

title: Path Traversal via Classpath Resource Loading
message: Path Traversal via Classpath Resource Loading

message: Sensitive Information Exposure via Model Attribute

title: Open Redirect Vulnerability

message: Exposure of Sensitive Environment Information

message: Potential Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via AsciiDoc Macro

message: Potential Path Traversal / Information Disclosure via Asciidoctor Macro

message: Inconsistent JSON escaping in AttackResult constructors

message: Potential Authorization Bypass via Username Manipulation

title: Potential Path Traversal / Unintended Resource Access
message: Potential Path Traversal / Unintended Resource Access

message: Open Redirect / Unsafe Forwarding

title: Potential NullPointerException leading to Denial of Service
message: Potential NullPointerException leading to Denial of Service

title: Potential NullPointerException in constructor
message: Potential NullPointerException in constructor

message: Sensitive Information Exposure via Environment Property

message: Insecure Authorization and Potential Data Loss via Unrestricted Lesson Reset

message: Potential IndexOutOfBoundsException leading to Denial of Service

title: Potential NullPointerException leading to Denial of Service
message: Potential NullPointerException leading to Denial of Service

message: Sensitive Information Exposure via Unauthenticated Endpoint

message: Sensitive data exposure via Lombok @Getter

message: SQL Injection via Schema Creation

message: Insecure use of Integer.valueOf() on user-controlled input

message: Improper Input Validation / Client-Side Restriction Bypass

message: Potential Regex Denial of Service (ReDoS)

title: Insecure Deserialization Risk
message: Insecure Deserialization Risk

title: Sensitive data exposure via toString() method
message: Sensitive data exposure via toString() method

message: Potential timing attack in string comparison

message: Potential Timing Attack on Flag Comparison

title: Potential Thread Safety Issue with Shared Mutable State
message: Potential Thread Safety Issue with Shared Mutable State

message: Hardcoded sensitive credential

message: Hardcoded Credentials / Sensitive Information Exposure

title: Potential ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException via Unsafe Array Manipulation
message: Potential ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException via Unsafe Array Manipulation

message: Insecure Random Number Generation for Security-Sensitive PIN

title: SQL Injection
message: SQL Injection

title: Sensitive Information Exposure via Path Traversal/Information Disclosure
message: Sensitive Information Exposure via Path Traversal/Information Disclosure

message: Use of Cryptographically Broken Hash Function (MD5)

title: Use of Cryptographically Weak Random Number Generator
message: Use of Cryptographically Weak Random Number Generator

message: Broken Access Control / Authentication Bypass via HTTP Verb Tampering

message: Sensitive Information Exposure in HTTP Header

message: Race condition in shared mutable state

title: Hardcoded sensitive coupon code
message: Hardcoded sensitive coupon code

message: Sensitive Data Exposure: Inclusion of SSN in API response

message: Sensitive data exposure via API endpoint

message: Use of insecure RSA public exponent

title: Use of Insecure Random Number Generator
message: Use of Insecure Random Number Generator

message: Use of insecure random number generator

message: Use of cryptographically weak hash function (MD5)

message: Hardcoded Cryptographic Secret/Hash
judge_reason: The application hardcodes a SHA-256 hash at line 36 to validate a secret, which is a hardcoded credential vulnerability in a production context.

message: Sensitive Data Exposure: Private Key returned in HTTP response

title: Hardcoded sensitive credential
message: Hardcoded sensitive credential

title: Potential NullPointerException due to unsafe string comparison
message: Potential NullPointerException due to unsafe string comparison

message: Sensitive Information Exposure via Exception Details

message: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Vulnerability

message: Insecure Deserialization of untrusted data

message: Insecure Deserialization of Untrusted Data

message: Insecure Session Management / Authentication Bypass via Cookie

message: Potential NullPointerException in equality check

message: Hardcoded cryptographic secret

title: datadog/java-xss
message: Source: The HTTP request method obtained via request.getMethod(). Sink: The conditional check at line 46 that restricts access based on the HTTP verb. judge_reason: @GetMapping restricts the endpoint to GET requests only. Spring Framework returns 405 for other verbs (POST/PUT) before method execution, making the bypass logic unreachable and CWE-79 non-existent.

title: datadog/java-xss

title: datadog/java-sqli
message: The code contains a secondary SQL injection vulnerability. Source: The user-controlled variable 'action' (passed as 'query' from the injectable method). judge_reason: User-controlled input is concatenated into a query, passed to 'log', and executed. Replacing single quotes with double quotes is insufficient to prevent SQL injection.

title: datadog/java-xss
message: Source: The 'action' parameter originated from user input via the SQL query string constructed in 'injectableQueryConfidentiality'. Sink: The 'statement.executeUpdate(logQuery)' call on line 142. Dataflow: The user-controlled SQL string is passed as 'action' to the 'log' method, where it is concatenated into a new SQL INSERT statement. Sanitization: The call `action.replace(''', '"')` is insufficient to prevent SQL injection, as other characters can still be used to break out of the string context in the INSERT statement. Therefore, this is a confirmed SQL Injection vulnerability.
judge_reason: Untrusted input 'name'/'auth_tan' reaches a manual SQL INSERT via the 'action' parameter. The 'replace' sanitization is insufficient to prevent injection in all SQL dialects/configurations.

title: datadog/java-xss

title: datadog/java-xss
message: Source: The @CurrentUsername annotation provides the username. Sink: The File constructor on line 32 takes the username as part of the file path. Dataflow: The untrusted username flows directly into the file path construction without validation. Sanitization: No sanitization is performed on the username. An attacker who can control their assigned username (e.g., via registration inputs) can use characters like '..' to perform a path traversal attack and write/overwrite files outside the intended directory. This is a path traversal vulnerability.
judge_reason: The username is concatenated directly into a file path without sanitization, allowing directory traversal if the identity provider or registration process permits path traversal characters in usernames.

title: datadog/java-xss
message: Source: multipartFile.getOriginalFilename() provides the untrusted filename from the user. Sink: destinationDir.toPath().resolve(...) at line 75, followed by Files.copy. Dataflow: The user-provided filename is joined with a base directory without path normalization or sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g., passing '..\/..\/file.txt'). No sanitization is performed on the filename before using it in resolve(). Conclusion: This is a confirmed path traversal vulnerability.
judge_reason: User-controlled filename from multipart upload is resolved against a base directory without validation, allowing path traversal via '../' sequences.
